findings.evidence: You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review.
findings.violation: Three consecutive sentences use three different terms, stipend item, reimbursable item, and covered purchase amount, for what appears to be the same underlying object, with no defined term or stated equivalence telling the reader whether the three name the same thing or three different things.
findings.fix: Pick one term for the item being reimbursed, for example stipend item, and use it consistently through this paragraph and the rest of the document, or state explicitly how the three terms differ.

findings.evidence: Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt.
findings.violation: This section restates how the request process begins, five sections after How to Apply's own opening step, employees start a stipend request in the benefits portal, and names a different starting point, confirming eligibility and an uploaded receipt, with no cross-reference between the two, so a reader cannot get one coherent picture of how the process starts without finding and reconciling two non-adjacent, apparently conflicting sections.
findings.fix: Merge this sentence into How to Apply, immediately after its opening step, or add a cross-reference explaining how the two starting points relate.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout.
findings.violation: The paragraph's opening sentence shares almost no vocabulary with the rest of the paragraph, so it does not preview the paragraph's actual topic.
findings.fix: Rewrite the opening sentence to state the topic the rest of the paragraph covers.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter.
findings.violation: The section's four sentences pursue four unrelated themes, stipend coordination, a past travel expense audit, federal remote work guidance, and the office coffee budget, with no signal connecting any of them, so a reader who finishes the section cannot state what it was about.
findings.fix: Remove the three sentences unrelated to stipend coordination, or move each to the section its own topic belongs in, so Program Coordination covers only stipend request coordination.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter.
findings.violation: Each sentence's subject shifts to something the previous sentence gave the reader no basis for, the benefits team, then a separate audit, then federal guidance, then the office coffee budget, so the reader has to re-orient at every sentence boundary instead of following one running topic.
findings.fix: Rewrite the paragraph so each sentence's subject picks up the topic the previous sentence just established, or delete the sentences that do not belong to this paragraph's topic.

findings.evidence: Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days. You track its status there until the payment clears.
findings.violation: The paragraph addresses the reader directly as you in the sentences before and after, but the middle sentence, an imperative with no stated subject, describes countersigning, an action the document elsewhere attributes to the manager rather than the employee, leaving the reader unable to tell from this sentence alone whether it is an instruction meant for them.
findings.fix: Name the actor explicitly, for example the manager countersigns the employee's request within two business days.

findings.evidence: Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing.
findings.violation: 3 comma-set-off clause(s) totalling 14 words intervene between the sentence's apparent subject and its verb.
findings.fix: Move the interrupting clause elsewhere, or split it into its own sentence.

findings.evidence: An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives. The...
findings.violation: The paragraph opens with none of the fixed transition words, so the reader is not told how it relates to the paragraph before it.
findings.fix: Open the paragraph with a transition word that states its relationship to the prior paragraph.

findings.evidence: Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt.
findings.violation: The series' 2 items mix grammatical forms (gerund, other) at their head words instead of sharing one form.
findings.fix: Restate every item in the series with the same grammatical form.

findings.evidence: The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out.
findings.violation: The sentence's newest and most important element, the 200 dollar review threshold, sits in the middle, while the sentence ends on before it pays out, information about the stipend process already established earlier in the document.
findings.fix: End the sentence on the threshold, for example, the finance office reviews a stipend request before it pays out when the request is over 200 dollars.
